question: A patient with AKI has the following values: serum Na 138 mEq/L, urine Na 12 mEq/L, serum creatinine 3.2 mg/dL, urine creatinine 180 mg/dL. What does the calculated FENa suggest, and in which clinical context is this result UNRELIABLE?

answers.text: FENa <1%, suggesting pre-renal AKI; unreliable in patients on diuretics

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. FENa = (urine Na × serum Cr) / (serum Na × urine Cr) = (12 × 3.2) / (138 × 180) = 38.4/24840 ≈ 0.15% — well below 1%, supporting pre-renal AKI. FENa is unreliable in diuretic use (diuretics force natriuresis, raising urine Na regardless of volume status), and also in contrast nephropathy and myoglobinuric AKI.

answers.text: FENa >2%, suggesting intrinsic renal AKI; unreliable in nephrotic syndrome

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The calculated FENa here is approximately 0.15% (<1%), indicating pre-renal physiology, not intrinsic AKI. Nephrotic syndrome is not the primary caveat for FENa unreliability.

answers.text: FENa <1%, suggesting pre-renal AKI; unreliable in patients with diabetic nephropathy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. While diabetic nephropathy can affect sodium handling, it is not the primary cited limitation of FENa. The main caveat is diuretic use, which forces renal sodium excretion and invalidates the <1% cut-off for pre-renal AKI.

answers.text: FENa >1%, suggesting intrinsic renal AKI; unreliable in AKI-on-CKD

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The FENa calculation from these values yields approximately 0.15%, which is <1% — this pattern suggests pre-renal AKI. The key limitation is diuretic use, not AKI-on-CKD per se.

overallFeedback.feedback: FENa = (urine Na × serum Cr)/(serum Na × urine Cr) = (12×3.2)/(138×180) ≈ 0.15% → <1% → pre-renal. Key limitation: unreliable in patients on diuretics (forced natriuresis invalidates the cut-off).

Correct. FENa ≈ 0.15% (<1%) = pre-renal. The most important clinical caveat: FENa is unreliable when the patient has received diuretics, because diuretics force renal Na wasting regardless of volume status.
